thread:
Priya (PM): quick sync — finalizing Q2 plan for Reserved Pools. Need decisions on: tier sizing (S/M/L), burst granularity (per-tenant vs pooled), and autoscale latency SLOs. I sketched acceptance criteria and launch gates below.
Sam (Eng): +1. Can you drop the acceptance criteria here? Curious about target p95/p99 for cold vs warm paths.
Priya (PM): pasted: 
- GA acceptance: stable throughput for committed capacity, documented failover to overflow pool, burst debt accounting, billing integration test, and per-tenant eviction behavior defined.
- SLOs proposed: 150ms p95 for warm requests, 400ms p95 for cold starts, p99 target 800ms warm.
Sam (Eng): warm path numbers look realistic. cold-start 400ms might be optimistic for some quantized models. Need perf matrix by model class.
Morgan (Infra): preemption model note: if we reserve headroom for bursts we need an eviction window. propose "soft-grace" 30s + preempt notify event so customers can retry. Also autoscale policy should prefer horizontal scale before preemption.
Jules (Sales): a few inbound prospects will only sign if we guarantee a minimum burst band for critical routes. They want per-route reserved burst (not just tenant-level). Is that doable within our pricing?
Eliza (CS): For onboarding GA, require a staging run: 48h of production-like traffic into reserved pool to validate eviction/preempt behavior. Also require docs for customer-run failover testing.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline: reserved-pools-autoscale v2 passed unit tests, failing integ tests in region-eu. See: https://ci.internal/reports/3101
Sam (Eng): technical constraint: we currently track burst credits at tenant granularity. Implementing per-route accounting would need schema change + billing pipeline updates. Est dev effort: 2 sprints. Alternative: route-tagging with priority buckets mapped to tenant credits.
Priya (PM): decision needed today: do we accept the 2-sprint effort for per-route burst or ship GA with tenant-level burst and explicit enterprise feature flag for per-route?
Jules (Sales): recommend enterprise flag. We can sell custom SLA pilots for top customers while GA covers tenant-level.
Morgan (Infra): agree enterprise flag. Also propose autoscale config snippet for discussion:
```json
{
  "policy": "latency_target",
  "target_p95_ms": 150,
  "scale_step": "add-nodes",
  "cooldown_s": 60,
  "burst_headroom_pct": 20
}
```
Sam (Eng): couple notes on that config: cooldown 60s is too aggressive for noisy traffic, suggest 120s. Also need hysteresis guard to avoid thrash.
Priya (PM): noted. Updated acceptance gate: autoscale configs validated under synthetic noise test (hysteresis + cooldown).
Eliza (CS): checklist item: billing integration test must validate credit reconciliation for bursts and refunds for preempted requests.
Jules (Sales): one more ask — marketing wants clear wording on what "guaranteed burst" means; define it in terms of headroom, duration, and measurable metric.
Priya (PM): action items: Sam/Morgan to produce perf matrix + updated autoscale config by EOD Thu; Eliza to draft onboarding runbook; Jules to prepare enterprise pilot pitch & pricing delta. We'll reconvene Fri 10am to lock the final GA criteria.
Sam (Eng): ack. I'll prototype per-route emulation with route tags so we can demo without schema changes.
Morgan (Infra): will add preempt notify event to the telemetry plan and schedule EU integ re-run.
Eliza (CS): I'll add the 48h staging run to the onboarding checklist and draft customer-facing failover play.
Jules (Sales): I'll flag top two prospects and line up pilot contracts.
Priya (PM): thanks team — goal is to have GA checklist stable by Fri and sign-off from Eng + CS. If anyone spots a blocker earlier, ping me in thread. :thumbsup:
